sections.h2: Which Union County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Union County keeps its tax offices together at the County Office Building, 233 West Sixth Street, Marysville, Ohio 43040. Three of them matter to a seller.

  • Auditor. Sets values, keeps the tax credits, runs the Board of Revision complaint process and stamps deeds. Phone 937-645-3003.
  • Treasurer. Mails bills and takes payment, with a drop box at the back entrance. Phone 937-645-3035, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., closed on federal holidays.
  • Recorder. Files the deed and any mortgage release after the auditor's stamp. Phone 937-645-3032.

The auditor's page puts the county at about 32,800 property records, and the treasurer's page describes more than 30,000 parcels. By the treasurer's account, roughly 70 percent of what the office collects goes to local schools.

sections.h2: How does Union County calculate a property tax bill?
sections.html:
The auditor sets a market value for each parcel, and the treasurer's FAQ says the assessed value is 35 percent of that figure. The assessed value is multiplied by the total tax rate for the parcel's district, then reduced by credits.

  • Residential and agricultural property gets a 10 percent credit on the net tax for levies passed before November 2013.
  • An owner-occupied home gets a further 2 1/2 percent credit on the home and up to one acre, but the owner must apply on form DTE 105C.
  • Levies passed after November 2013 that raise funding do not carry the rollbacks.
  • The Homestead Exemption adds a reduction for owners aged 65 or older and the permanently disabled, and since 2014 it uses an income test.

Ohio caps unvoted taxation at ten mills per thousand dollars of assessed value, and any levy beyond that needs a vote. The county's tax rate page lists rates by district and levy, and the DTE 515 report gives the composite reduction factors. To find your own rate, search the parcel on the auditor's site and open the “Where your taxes go” link. The first two digits of the parcel number identify the tax district.

Where a house sits matters for schools. The auditor's GIS notes that when a district line crosses a house, the school district where the master bedroom is located governs the whole house.

sections.h2: When are Union County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in January and June, and Ohio collects a year behind. A bill that arrives in 2026 covers tax year 2025. The county sets each year's dates, and the treasurer's FAQ says the first half usually falls in mid-February and the second half in mid-July or August. The county's 2026 schedule is below.

Union County treasurer calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026
DateWhat happened or applies
February 18, 2026First half due
February 19 and 28, 20265 percent, then 10 percent penalty added to unpaid first half

Source: Union County Treasurer payment information.

A payment mailed with a postmark on or before the due date counts as on time, but a private meter mark does not. The treasurer also notes that not receiving a bill is no excuse. Before the second half came due in 2026, the treasurer advised paying only the first half, because House Bill 186 required rates to be recalculated for the second half. The treasurer said overpayments would be credited or refunded.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Union County tax bill, or spread it out?
sections.html:
Checks go to the Union County Treasurer at the Sixth Street address, by mail, in person or in the back drop box. The county takes cards and e-checks online, and the treasurer's FAQ says a processing fee goes to the payment vendor rather than the county. In 2026 the treasurer also accepted payments at a Richwood bank on set days before each due date, so check the payment information page for any such location.

Two programs help with budgeting:

  • Real Estate Tax Escrow Program. You prepay monthly, and the money is applied when each half comes due.
  • Delinquent payment plan. A written contract with the treasurer lets you pay back taxes in installments while keeping current tax paid. Penalty and interest are held in escrow and removed once the contract is paid off, and added back if you default.

If a bill goes unpaid, a delinquent notice is mailed in late September or early October, and the name appears on the delinquent tax list in the local paper. If the tax is still unpaid the next November, it is certified to the county prosecutor to start foreclosure.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Union County valuation?
sections.html:
A complaint goes to the county auditor, who presents it to the Board of Revision. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 allows the complaint until the later of March 31 or the close of first-half collection, and the county's FAQ states a window from January 1 through March 31 of the following year.

  • File a notarized DTE Form 1 by email, fax or mail to the Auditor's Office, Attn: Board of Revision, at the Sixth Street address.
  • Contest only the current tax year. The board does not look back.
  • Attach a closing statement, purchase contract, escrow statement and deed if you bought or sold recently.
  • Hearing dates follow the order in which complaints are received.
  • A property held by a business or trust should use an attorney. An individual does not need one.

If the change you seek tops $50,000 in market value (or $17,500 assessed), the school board is notified. Board decisions are held for 30 days, and a refund or credit follows about sixty days after that. An appeal goes to the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals on DTE Form 4 or to the Court of Common Pleas within 30 days of the decision letter. In many cases a decision holds until the next triennial update. The auditor reports the last full reappraisal in 2019, with updates every third year after.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs does Union County offer?
sections.html:
Besides the rollbacks above, the auditor administers two programs that a buyer or seller may ask about.

  • Homestead Exemption. The county page lists age 65 or older, permanent disability, or a surviving spouse aged 59 to 64 of a person already receiving the exemption. The applicant must own and live in the home, and apply by the first Monday in June. Disabled veterans use form DTE 105I. Ask the auditor for the current income cap.
  • Current Agricultural Use Value (CAUV). Farmland of ten or more acres in commercial agriculture for three years can be taxed on its farm income value. A parcel under ten acres needs $2,500 average yearly gross income. The application must reach the auditor after the first Monday in January and before the first Monday in March. Leaving the program brings a charge equal to three years of tax savings.

When a property sells, section 319.202 asks the grantee to affirm whether the seller said the property carried a rollback or CAUV status. A seller with CAUV land should talk to the auditor before closing about the recoupment charge.

sections.h2: What happens to property tax when you sell a Union County home?
sections.html:
Taxes are normally prorated between buyer and seller at closing, and the seller stops being responsible after that. If a bill for a sold property still arrives, the treasurer asks you to forward it to the new owner or call so a corrected bill can be prepared. Look at the settlement statement, since a bill for the prior year can come due after you have moved.

The county is growing quickly. The Census Bureau puts the 2025 population at 73,446, up 17.0 percent from the 2020 base, with a median owner-occupied home value of $344,900 and 968 building permits in 2025. Marysville Exempted Village, Fairbanks, North Union, Triad, Jonathan Alder, Buckeye Valley, Elgin, Benjamin Logan and Dublin City serve the county's school districts.

Ask the title company to pull current and delinquent tax status, and ask the treasurer for the tax rate sheet for your district before you set a price.

faqs.q: When are Union County property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is usually due in mid-February and the second half in mid-July or August, and the treasurer sets the exact dates each year. In 2026 the first half was due February 18 and the second half August 12.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late Union County tax payment?
faqs.a: The treasurer's 2026 schedule added 5 percent the day after the due date and 10 percent about ten days later. Interest on prior-year delinquency starts on September 1, with further interest on December 1.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Union County property value?
faqs.a: File a notarized Board of Revision complaint with the County Auditor between January 1 and March 31 of the year after the tax year. It can be emailed, faxed or mailed to the Auditor's Office at 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Union County taxes monthly?
faqs.a: Yes. The Real Estate Tax Escrow Program lets you prepay on a monthly basis, and the treasurer applies the funds when each half comes due. Contact the treasurer's office to enroll.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Union County home sells?
faqs.a: Closing normally prorates the tax between buyer and seller. After closing, the buyer is responsible for any tax that comes due. If a bill still goes to the old owner, forward it to the buyer or ask the treasurer to reissue it.
